data.title: Casamigos World Cup 2026

summary.text: Bringing Casamigos bottle personalisation to the FIFA World Cup 26™ through the latest iteration of our scalable, AI-powered Halo platform.

description.text: Our partnership with Casamigos has taken us from ski seasons to California beaches. To kick-off the FIFA World Cup 26™, we joined forces to deliver a vibrant activation that lets fans turn their supporter pride into memento bottles for them and their crew.

We combined the craft of our hand-drawn illustration with the limitless imagination of our Halo personalisation platform, training our custom-built AI engine on an exclusive collection of original artworks. The experience invites fans to hand-pick their own colourways based on team pride or personal preference, guiding them through a series of playful match-day questions with real-time design feedback so they can see exactly how their answers shape their bottle. To truly capture a moment in time, users can even emblazon their bottle with a live-updating score from the exact game they attended or celebrated.

Our end-to-end delivery encompasses everything from the initial strategic framework and intuitive UX/UI design to pioneering the enterprise-level platform that drives the experience. The system was rolled out across FIFA fan activations in New York and New Jersey, a dedicated trailer tour across the West Coast of the United States, and online via TheBar.com. We were able to simultaneously meet fans at the event, and roll out a pioneering e-commerce opportunity, allowing fans to experience AI personalisation at scale. The final bottle is a genuinely personalised keepsake, shaped by each fan’s experience and the moments that made their tournament memorable.

Highlights – Our Halo platform, coupled with handcrafted icons, played a huge role in helping Casamigos bring consumer personalisation to The FIFA World Cup 26™ like never before. The experience also marks a landmark moment for e-commerce AI personalisation opportunities.

data.title: AI Quests

summary.text: A groundbreaking learning platform that blends academia and industry expertise to inspire teens around the world through playable experiences.

description.text: From climate change to food security, AI has the potential to address some of humanity’s biggest challenges. But, for this to happen, we must inspire a new generation of AI changemakers and prepare the middle schoolers of today to change lives through responsible AI deployment. Fusing cutting-edge Google Research projects with pedagogical expertise from Stanford University, AI Quests is a fully immersive, interactive learning experience that shows students the wonder of what’s possible.

Research shows students’ performance can improve 50% when a subject is gamified. Spurred on by this insight, we collaborated closely with Google Research and Stanford to develop an exciting world of playable AI quests — with Quests 1 & 2 fully localised into 11 languages — inviting students to follow in the footsteps of real AI researchers by exploring AI technology and learning to deploy it responsibly.

Every aspect of our simulated planet was designed to let students see the impact of their actions. From the rich variety of environments to the weird and wonderful creatures who inhabit them, we wanted students to experience firsthand how AI can augment human decisions, as well as understanding the importance of ethical, informed use.

Each mission is introduced by a primary character, with their own deeply developed backstory, regional history and lore. In Market Marshes, we meet Luna, a part-amphibian part-moss-like creature born from her marshland environment. Working with Stanford, we created Luna and her story specifically to encourage empathy from the students, which in turn helps them to build a genuine sense of mission and desire to help. This emotional involvement leads to more engaged learning, a better understanding of the subject, and real inspiration to consider how else AI might be able to solve real-world problems.

We used Google AI throughout the development process, from environment and character creation to voiceovers. The environments combine Gemini-generated imagery with a layer of custom 3D assets, modelled and optimised before being exported to WebGL. By instancing key objects across the scenes, we kept the performance high and the file size low. Each model was brought to life with our custom toon shader in WebGL pulling colour directly from the vertex and colour attribute data. An additional dimension that was crucial to building an immersive experience was sound. We carefully crafted and layered both ambient sound and soundtracks to bring our environments to life; adding spot sounds to offer extra guidance and feedback.

By bringing together Google’s deep technical expertise and Stanford’s knowledge of learning processes, we’ve been able to create something truly original: a platform that democratises innovation. A place that doesn’t just educate students on the uses of AI, but gives them space to imagine new frontiers of advancement. Frontiers they’ll one day, hopefully, be a part of.

The second quest, Dusky Dunes, takes players to a desert landscape where inhabitants are suffering from a UV-related eye disease. Here they meet Dr Visus (an eye specialist) and their assistant Arlo, who have been struggling to diagnose and treat rising numbers of patients in their region. Together with Professor Skye’s guidance, they invite players to build an AI model that can help in early diagnosis

In this quest, the primary learning objective is to show how AI-powered diagnostic tools can help doctors address healthcare challenges in underserved communities. As a result, the Dusky Dunes’ sound, lighting and visual treatment were designed to reflect geographically remote and nomadic environments inspired by Mongolia, the Sahara, Patagonia and Northern Africa.

Additionally, the Dusky Dunes campsite environment is a transient and ephemeral setting intended specifically to set up another core learning focus within this quest – the need for diversity in data when training AI models. Every aspect of the 3D environment, from packable tents to lightweight camping objects, allowed us to tell a deeper story and introduce diverse characters traversing through the desert lands.

summary.text: Uniting expressive brand storytelling and intelligent guidance for two YouTube brand platforms.

description.text: To support YouTube as they implemented their latest brand evolution, we created a new Brand Standards website to house and express it with clarity and confidence. The platform transforms enterprise infrastructure into a design-led, immersive destination powered by dual navigation and a WebGL-driven landing experience.

Alongside the site, we crafted a Gemini-powered Brand Assistant that replaces a static, time-intensive query form with instant, precise guidance. The aim was to reduce the time YouTube’s brand management team spend dealing with 7k requests a year, while also offering a more engaging experience for visitors. We translated the refreshed identity across an expansive index of brand expressions, all housed within a modular design system.

Lens-based navigation lets users compare expressions across product areas without leaving the page, applying guidance from the selected area instantly. Helpfulness is built into every interaction, with quick links and actions like ‘click to copy’. Bold and witty, we let the voice and visuals speak for themselves, with seamless UX amplifying the brand-world immersion.
Highlights – A first-of-its-kind custom CMS build paired with intelligent automation, empowering 2.7 billion monthly users and 113 mil channels with instant, on-brand clarity at global scale.

data.title: That Rightmove Filter

summary.text: Generating engagement for the UK’s number one property website through a ground-breaking AI experience

description.text: In an ambitious debut for our new partnership with the UK’s number one property website, Rightmove, we went big. Combining the power of AI with the iconic Rightmove brand, we created a spectacular digital brand experience where people could take a selfie, pick their theme and generate their most outrageous dream homes.

Our goal was to demonstrate Rightmove’s unmatched catalogue of homes in a fun, shareable experience. Through the unbelievable range of fantastic homes that can be generated, we communicated how there really is a home for everyone in a fun, tongue-in-cheek kind of way, bringing to life Rightmove’s brand line ‘Believe it’.

Powering the experience is our groundbreaking, custom-built AI engine called Maniphest. Developed in-house by Phantom to generate high-quality, brand-aligned images at a massive scale – no mean feat in itself – Maniphest combines cutting-edge AI generation models with our proprietary face-swapping technology to seamlessly embed the user in unique AI-generated images.

To enable users to personalise their experience, we created four categories – each containing three subcategories – to choose from. Using AI not just to generate images, but to filter and sort them into categories based on their aesthetic and quality is a breakthrough AI workflow, helping communicate Rightmove as a dynamic, innovative brand at the forefront of technology.
Highlights – And as for results? Watch this space…

data.title: Stranger Things Walking Tour

summary.text: Transporting fans into an immersive digital world for the final adventure

description.text: In anticipation of the grand finale of Stranger Things, we helped Netflix bring the magic to fans in London, transforming them into Hawkins Heroes on their own final adventure. Via an interactive, engaging web app, we created a parallel world in the heart of the city for users to navigate and pick up exclusive digital collectables – and even collect real-world prizes.

Centred on London’s bustling Oxford Street in the week leading up to the finale, the experience is spread across six partner stores. Activated by QR code, the app provides fans with a map and a digital backpack, allowing them to pick up Hawkins-inspired collectables along the way, and to share them on their socials. Reflecting iconic items from the Stranger Things story, each piece was meticulously modelled in 3D in-house at Phantom. Collecting all six enters the user in the draw for Stranger Things prizes, including VIP experiences, tickets to the stage play, backstage tours and cast meet-and-greets.

To further build excitement and link the digital and physical realms, the first 250 fans to visit each store each day were given a code to redeem via a themed vending machine dispensing physical goodies like pins, badges and keychains.

data.title: Virtual Try-On

summary.text: An immersive virtual try-on experience that lets users explore Loop’s full range from home.

description.text: Loop’s Virtual Try-On reimagines how sound can be experienced online. We transformed their product discovery journey into an interactive, sensory experience, letting users hear the difference between each pair of earplugs before they buy. Blending sound-reactive visuals with intuitive interaction, the experience brings Loop’s commitment to design and performance to life in a way that’s as beautiful as it is functional.

We crafted a mobile-first interactive experience that lets customers virtually hear and see the effect of Loop’s earplugs across five products, bringing clarity and confidence to their choice. A responsive WebGL gradient reacts to sound frequency, visually translating how each product filters or reduces noise in real time.

Built directly into Loop’s Shopify ecosystem, the experience merges audio precision with digital artistry through GSAP and Three.js. Each soundscape reflects real-world use cases, turning an everyday purchase into an immersive, sensory moment that feels both informative and thoughtfully on-brand.
Highlights – Launched simultaneously across three global stores, the Virtual Try-On set a new digital benchmark for product immersion, soon expanding to more of Loop’s range.

data.title: Doja Cat: Club Vie

summary.text: Building a world of after-hours alchemy to give Doja Cat’s fifth album the ultimate digital launch party.

description.text: From the intergalactic fantasies of Planet Her, to the neon haze of the 1980s, our work with Doja Cat is always pushing boundaries. For her fifth studio album, Vie, we devised a WebGL-powered wild night out that enticed fans from the boudoir to the dance floor.

Fans' data formed the basis for a virtual guestlist. Doja superfans were able to bypass the fierce bouncers and enter Club Vie before anyone else, giving those good girls and boys early access to exclusive track previews. Using WebGL, we allowed fans to control the track previews by spinning the disco ball, adding a deliciously tactile element. We built the dance floor, dancers, disco ball, and smoke effect separately to replicate the entrancing, hectic atmosphere of a real club. Hidden among the clickable easter eggs is a message from Doja herself, but you’ll have to find that for yourself… au revoir.

In the lead up to the main event, we designed and built a 3D holding scene to fuel excitement. The room was complete with a glowing vanity mirror where fans could scrawl messages in sultry strokes of cherry-red lipstick; creating a daring digital confessional.

Objects in the room teased themes from the album to ramp up anticipation, such as a Sony Walkman from which a muted track snippet could be heard playing. By accessing this first phase of the experience, visitors were guaranteed entry to Clue Vie, which we teased with an invite laying on the dressing table.

data.title: Season's Treatings

summary.text: Reimagining festive gingerbread baking as a playful act of co-creation, powered by the latest Nano Banana Pro.

description.text: Every year, our relationships with partners old and new ignite our imaginations and drive us to push the boundaries of what’s possible in technology creative. To wrap up 2025, we wanted an extra special gift that everyone could enjoy – and a traditional gingerbread just wasn’t cutting it.
Not only did we send artfully presented IRL gingerbread dudes to our partners, we created a complementary digital world for them to explore.

When Google DeepMind released Gemini 3 Pro Image (aka Nano Banana Pro) in November, we immediately began experimenting. Built on the Gemini 3 Pro reasoning engine, the ability to combine high-fidelity, 4K image generation with real creative logic offers a tech playground. What we were most excited about was the possibility of combining this technology with real-world products.

We explored retail possibilities by combining supermarket product images from Tesco with text prompts. Users can select nostalgic faves like “silver pearls” or “foam shrimp,” and the system feeds these product shots as partial prompts to the Vertex AI Gemini API. We love how this transforms AI into a curator of reality, creating imaginative arrangements of real sweets rather than inventing new ones.
For us, there were two huge benefits to the latest Gemini Image model:

14-Input Unlock: it handles up to 14 visual references at once, enabling precise blending of multiple product images. This allows us to feed the model the exact visual data of multiple ingredient product images (the precise texture of a Tesco chewy gummies, the glint of a colourful sprinkle) alongside structural guides.

Deep Think Reasoning: it separates structure from texture, ensuring objects function realistically while allowing creative designs. It understands that a "banana gummy" selected as a "limb" must function structurally like an arm, rather than just appearing as a floating picture of a banana.

The model's temperature settings and generative capabilities ensure that no two gingerbread creations are identical, even with the same ingredients. This sweet spot between surprise and control captures the fun of AI-assisted creativity and creates a collectible quality. For an extra layer of delight, each gingerbread comes with a shoppable recipe for recreating at home – turning users’ creations into something tangible.
We’re so excited to see how we can continue to push AI from an experimental tool to an essential component of competitive retail strategy in 2026.

data.title: Stop and Search

summary.text: A search-powered campaign inviting the UK to confront systemic racism through self-led discovery and honest learning.

description.text: Systemic racism isn’t just an issue across the Atlantic. From healthcare to policing, racial inequalities exist in the UK too, but they’re often overlooked. We wanted to challenge that by turning online searches into a tool for education, revealing the everyday discrimination faced by people of colour in the UK.

We identified 15 search terms that expose key areas of systemic racism, from biases in healthcare to policing and education. Using bold, disruptive visuals inspired by the Black Lives Matter movement, then taking our message to the streets of London with flyposters and stickers, driving curiosity and action.

The campaign was amplified across social media, urging people to stop and search these terms for themselves. The response was incredible, with London BLM sharing our post, sparking wider discussion, and driving thousands of visits to our website. Within weeks, the campaign gained traction across multiple platforms, proving the power of a simple search to open eyes and shift narratives.
Highlights – London BLM’s Instagram share drove a wave of visits in the first week, with continued social shares and media coverage expanding the conversation even further.

Designed as a satirical, interactive museum, the experience showcases a series of exhibits featuring the worst customer service encounters. Visitors navigate a world of painfully familiar frustrations, from an impossible rhythm game that keeps customers on hold to a CAPTCHA challenge that never quite believes you are human.

The more annoying the experience, the more effective it became. The museum playfully highlighted the daily frustrations of bad customer service, making Zendesk’s vision of a seamless future feel all the more urgent. Its intentionally infuriating but exceptionally crafted design and build resonated widely, earning multiple converted awards and accolades.

Highlights – The experience had incredible engagement, with visitors spending an average of 2.54 minutes per session, rising to over four minutes for those interacting with at least one exhibit. data.title: Petra

summary.text: Bringing the wonder of Petra to the world with an immersive VR experience that redefines how history is explored and remembered.

description.text: Petra has captured imaginations for centuries, but few can witness its beauty in person. In collaboration with Google, we created a virtual experience that gives people everywhere a chance to explore the UNESCO World Heritage site in extraordinary detail, unlocking new ways to discover one of the world’s most iconic places.

Expanding on our early innovations in web-based VR, we designed a deeply immersive journey that combines cinematic visuals, spatial audio, fluid navigation and interactive storytelling. Every element was crafted to draw users into Petra’s hidden corners and historic grandeur, guided by a rich audio narrative that reveals the legacy of the Nabataeans.

More than a virtual tour, the experience sparked global attention with over one million visitors in its first week. description.text: For Google Store’s biggest sale of the year, we created Shopper Hopper - a nostalgic arcade game that transformed Black Friday into an interactive adventure. With high-speed gameplay, immersive design, and a buildable arcade cabinet, it became a shopping experience unlike any other.

Bringing the magic of gaming into the real world, Black Friday shoppers also received a build-your-own arcade cabinet, transforming their smartphones into mini retro consoles for a fully immersive experience.

Beyond just a game, Shopper Hopper became a flexible platform for engagement. Following its success, we adapted it for a B2B audience in MENA, refreshing its colour palette, redesigning characters, and turning power-ups into Google products that showcased real business solutions. The result was an endlessly playable experience that spanned audiences, markets, and mediums.

Highlights – With over 3,000 players across 90 countries and an average engagement time of over five minutes, Shopper Hopper drove both consumer and business engagement for Google’s biggest shopping moment.

Centred around an interactive home, Home Truths guides users through a day in their life, surfacing the hidden impact of their daily habits. A rich, real-time web experience, the project balances sophistication with warmth. Dynamic lighting evolves with the passing hours, while advanced shadow rendering using PCSS algorithms creates a soft, natural aesthetic. Web Audio API integration enhances immersion, reinforcing key moments with responsive sound design. The result is an experience that invites curiosity, rewards exploration, and makes sustainability feel deeply personal.

description.text: Teaming up with Google Play for their incredible sponsorship of Zedd in The Park, we transformed the highly anticipated festival into an interactive experience that would live far beyond the event itself. Coming to life as a fast-paced mobile game, we invited top Play members to race through action-packed levels, immersing themselves in the festival no matter where they were playing from.

Capturing Zedd In The Park’s frenetic energy, we created an end-to-end and hyper-engaging series of backdrops inspired by the festival's monumental IRL Playground installation. Ensuring the game felt like a true extension of the festival's spirit, we took our lead from the Playground's real-world activities and developed a multi-level track that takes players on an adventure through mini-golf, a lookout tower, and a slide.

Heavily inspired by the golden age of 8 and 16-bit gaming, we used a mix of modern techniques to dial up nostalgia, mixing zany playscapes and dynamic neon lighting, replicating the incredible vibes for fans near and far. Hundreds of thousands of players across the US raced through obstacle-filled levels, collecting Play Points and winning big along the way.

summary.text: A pioneering VR adventure, exploring the legend of Europe's highest mountain.

description.text: Scaling Mont Blanc is a monumental feat. We embraced the challenge, partnering with Google to craft a revolutionary VR experience that democratised access to this iconic peak, pushing the boundaries of what was achievable within a web browser while bringing the mountain to the masses.

Built for Google Cardboard, the experience takes users on a breathtaking journey up Mont Blanc, guided by High Mountain Guide Patrick Gabarrou. Through an intuitive UI inspired by smart ski goggles, climbers can monitor altitude, temperature, and vitals while exploring the mountain’s key routes. Each stage of the ascent is brought to life through stunning 360° panoramas, explorable 3D hotspots, and rich audio-visual storytelling, curated from an extraordinary archive of assets captured directly on the mountain.

Delivering virtual reality at scale within a web browser was a major technical feat. We optimized performance across devices, balancing high-fidelity visuals with a smooth user experience on both Android and iOS. The experience seamlessly integrates multiple layers of interactivity, with 11 explorable scenes and over 50 embedded points of interest. The result is a fully immersive journey that pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in mobile VR.

Highlights – A multi-award-winning experience that helped pioneered in-browser WebVR. Making a journey previously exclusive to expert climbers accessible on any smartphone, brought the beauty of Mont Blanc to millions.

description.text: We created Free Spirits Center as a fully-imagined digital wellness space for Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso’s latest release. Built as a playful, satirical journey through a serene clinic, the experience invites users into a delightfully unhinged world of absurd therapies and strange diagnoses, poking fun at “wellness that only works sometimes”.

An intake form asks users to ponder questions like “How do you feel about stillness?”, before offering an immersive prescription that teases track snippets from the album. Following a creative pivot away from architectural 3D spaces, we developed an abstract Therapy Void centred around a responsive orb visualiser and restrained graphic language that sat somewhere between wellness branding, performance art and internet chaos. Built on a flexible development framework and powered by a scalable weighted scoring system, the experience remained highly adaptable throughout production while delivering personalised, surreal outcomes.

To ensure participation felt playful throughout, we embedded date capture directly into the creative concept. Each answer feeds the surreal logic of the experience, while receiving real-world information about the album launch. Interactions were carefully refined to remove unnecessary friction, balancing ridiculous therapies and immersive engagement with an experience that remained intuitive and accessible.
Highlights – It was a positive reaction from the fans, leading to an immediate uplift in engagement across social channels.

In contrast to the fast-moving world of AI, the experience gave users space to pause, breathe, and explore at their own pace; transforming complex AI decisions into approachable journeys. Gentle motion design nudges users through the experience, allowing them to upskill in a truly inspirational environment.

Armed with learnings from our latest experiments, we took on a new challenge: simultaneously creating festive bottle design for both Johnnie Walker Black and Johnnie Walker Blue. It was important that both options felt premium, while still differentiating the offer.

For Johnnie Walker Black, an elevated everyday dram, we built a concept around the idea of a warm, inviting bar providing refuge in the winter – cold air misting the windows. We originally experimented with white ink snowflakes on the bottle glass, before realising more intricate patterns were even more visually appealing. In the end, we created timeless bauble-style patterns, frosted straight onto the glass.

For Johnnie Walker Blue, a blend for extraordinary occasions, we explored ideas around luxury. What’s more luxurious than sipping from a delicate cut-crystal glass? The delicate diamond-shaped patterns on traditional whisky tumblers are reminiscent of snowflakes, and we loved the playfulness of making the bottle look like a drinking glass.

data.title: Transforming Business

summary.text: Transforming winning Google Cloud strategies into a cinematic game that uses immersive, AI-powered videos to put players in C-suite roles.

description.text: Transforming Business is a groundbreaking playable film experience created to uniquely showcase Google Cloud products to a Financial Times audience. Players step into a year in the life of one of four C-suite leaders at the fictional Sunrise Cereals, navigating five high-pressure business decisions. The experience unfolds in first person, a choice designed to heighten immersion.

Mirroring the real pressures faced by today’s executives, a live share price reacts in real time to every decision. By combining raw strategic thinking with the emotional weight of leadership, the experience drives stronger recall and a deeper connection to the realities of modern business.

To bring each defining business moment to life, we built a bespoke AI filmmaking workflow that gave us complete creative control. Using Imagen, Nano Banana Pro and Veo, we built consistent environments, characters and narratives, directing camera movement, pacing and perspective. We created a holistic world for each character, thinking of their home, pets, and desk set-up to ensure the game feels endlessly playable, with meaningful differences between each story.

At the end of the game, players have an ‘annual review’, which assesses the business impact of their actions – a relatable nod to our audience. This touches on key career highlights, clearly connecting them to core cloud products and how well these were used during critical moments.
Highlights - A category-defining executive experience that reimagines how cloud capability is understood, replacing abstraction with agency, immersion and strategic clarity.

data.title: Google Visitor Experience Guide

summary.text: Blending digital wayfinding with one of the first public uses of 3D Google Maps to create a series of choose-your-own-adventure trails for Mountain View visitors.

description.text: Back in 2023, we supported Google’s pivotal public opening of their Mountain View campus by translating their ethos of innovation and community into an end-to-end brand identity. Now, we’ve created an enhanced digital guide that combines wayfinding with light gamification to take visitors of all ages on an even richer journey, tailored to their interests.

The experience needed to be intuitive for first-time guests, engaging for returning visitors, and scalable enough to grow with the campus for years to come. Life-sized artworks facilitated by Burning Man Project and local creators quickly became anchor points for exploration, alongside pop-up shops and thoughtfully designed communal spaces. Using users’ devices' geo-location capabilities in combination with Google’s Routes API, we were able to give directions to points of interest from anywhere on the campus — allowing visitors to start their journey whenever they wanted or even switch routes mid-journey.

As well as planning different routes around key landmarks, we added scannable QR codes to objects and signs to bring up more information and unlock a digital collectible sticker when visitors mark them as ‘discovered’. Not only does this create enrichment moments (and lots of fun for those with kids), it offers a sense of momentum and motivation to visitors as they move through their journey.
Highlights – Hundreds of visitors completed tours in the first week alone, marking a scalable, fully accessible digital experience powered by pioneering use of 3D Google Maps.

To land this in the most intriguing way possible, we decided that rather than simply shouting about Zendesk’s AI, we would turn the camera on fictional (yet highly relatable) AI. Each embodied the antithesis of Zendesk’s product differentiators and let them do the talking for us - highlighting how  Zendesk gets it right by showing what happens when customer service AI goes very, very wrong.

Viewers meet characters that were built to embody a specific AI failure - from Derek the well-meaning but useless chatbot, MEBO the arrogant know-it-all, Serenit-E the high-maintenance diva and SCR33CH an internet-trained disaster. Created entirely in-house, the campaign combined sharp writing, expressive animation, and motion capture to bring each AI to life. What started as a simple social campaign became a runaway success, earning millions of views and proving that even in a conversation as crowded as AI, creativity still wins.
Highlights – A standout campaign winning millions of views and setting Zendesk to create real cut-through in the AI conversation.

data.title: Ghosts of Christmas Cards

summary.text: Our AI Christmas card generator, blending nostalgia and tech for a viral holiday moment.

description.text: Nothing says Christmas like awkward family portraits and over-the-top festive cheer. For the holidays, we created Ghosts of Christmas Cards - an AI-powered card generator that transformed selfies into gloriously kitsch retro images. Instantly nostalgic, slightly unhinged, and endlessly shareable, it became an instant viral holiday hit.

The best viral experiences are quick, simple, and just weird enough to be irresistible. With Ghosts of Christmas Cards, users uploaded a selfie, picked an era, and our AI delivered a gloriously tacky Christmas card that felt straight out of a family photo album in seconds. Right down to the festive jumpers and soft-focus lighting.

To keep things feeling fresh, we built an experience optimised for quick interactions and repeat plays. Every card felt like a unique relic from Christmas past, from 80s studio glamour shots to 90s department store portraits. The experience exploded as hundreds of thousands of users shared their results across the world, landing a segment on BBC Radio and filling social feeds with nostalgic festive joy.
Highlights – 2.4 million visits from over 500,000 users in five days, peaking at 1.35 million views on Christmas Day, with viral shares from E.L. James, Greg James, Goldie, and Marcus Butler.

To get started, fans boarded InterstellHER Air where their Spotify listening habits determined their class - ranging from ‘So High’ first class to ‘Bottom Bitch’ cargo hold. As the album release approached, fans scanned their pass and launched through an interactive wormhole, arriving at the vibrant Planet Her. Suspended above its dreamlike terrain, inspired by Doja’s ‘Kiss Me More’ video, they explored the world while unlocking exclusive track snippets, making them some of the first to experience the album.
Highlights – With record-breaking fan engagement, Visit Planet Her became one of Sony Music’s most successful digital campaigns, sparking viral fan frenzy and earning an FWA Site of the Day award.

data.title: Puffer AW23

summary.text: Blowing up Superdry’s iconic puffer on socials.

description.text: Superdry’s puffer jacket is an icon. For their AW23 campaign, we reimagined it in a bold, digitally-led series of high-impact social films. Merging real-world locations with striking 3D animation, we transformed the jacket into a larger-than-life statement that demanded attention on social feeds.

To capture the jacket in perfect detail, we used photogrammetry and lidar scanning, creating a near-exact digital replica with rich, textured realism. Taking to the streets of London with the Superdry team, we scouted striking liminal spaces to seamlessly blend 3D animations with dynamic urban environments. For even greater realism, ambient lighting conditions were captured through HDRI technology, allowing us to meticulously match the lighting within our 3D scenes, ensuring a natural integration of digital elements with the real-world.

From jackets expanding beyond the skyline to playful animations of the Superdry logo and unexpected visual moments, every element was designed to grab attention mid-scroll. Both surreal and believably real, the response was immediate. The campaign took over social feeds, driving engagement that far exceeded expectations and cementing Superdry’s reputation for bold, fashion-forward storytelling in a perfect fusion of technical and creative craft.
Highlights – The visually striking social campaign doubled Superdry’s content output and reached 1.6 million views in just three days.

data.title: A Blend of Artistry

summary.text: The first-ever AI-powered whisky personalisation experience in collaboration with renowned Scottish artist Scott Naismith.

description.text: In a boundary-pushing project bringing together creative expertise across Phantom, Johnnie Walker and Diageo’s Breakthrough Innovation team, we crafted the first-ever AI-powered whisky personalisation experience. Using generative AI, whisky enthusiasts can co-create their own bottle of Blue Label with renowned Scottish artist Scott Naismith, each design truly one-of-a-kind: a highly individualised, never-to-be-replicated keepsake.

At the heart of the experience is a groundbreaking new technology called ‘Halo’. This innovative capability empowers consumers to leverage the power of generative AI to co-create designs for products in a way that is bespoke to them and relevant to the worlds they’re passionate about. Brands have allowed drinks fans to customise their bottles before – think classic name and date engravings – but never like this.

Hosted at Johnnie Walker’s flagship Princes Street location during the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, whisky fans were invited to answer a short series of questions via a purpose-built tablet questionnaire, giving our AI engine a flavour of their personalities. These were then blended with Scott’s vibrant, colourful abstractions, generating three unique designs for the visitor to choose from, illustrated in vivid detail on a custom-made 3D model, to be printed right there in-store.

Highlights –  All bottles quickly sold out, leading to a 113% year-on-year sales uplift for Johnnie Walker Blue Label. The experience generated 58+ pieces of press coverage with an estimated 12 million views and was rated 9.7/10 by Trend Hunter.

data.title: Ancient Greeks

summary.text: Bringing ancient Greek artifacts to life through dynamic experiential storytelling.

hero.alt_tag: Detailed relief sculpture from ancient Greece, showing bearded male figures in dynamic poses battling large, stylized snakes. One man grips a snake's neck, another wields a sword, amidst a crowded scene of figures engaged in combat.

description.text: When the Auckland War Memorial Museum hosted Ancient Greeks: Athletes, Warriors, and Heroes, a collection of over 170 treasured artefacts from the British Museum,they saw an opportunity to enhance the experience with digital storytelling. We created four projection-mapped animations that brought ancient Greek pottery and sculptures to life, revealing the myths, legends, and daily life of this extraordinary civilisation.

By combining 3D animation, 2D illustration, and carefully placed projections, we transformed amphorae and friezes into animated storytelling canvases. Javelin throwers vaulted across vases, warriors sailed between broken amphora shards in epic battles, and mythical figures emerged from marble friezes.

Each projection was designed to seamlessly interact with the artefacts, creating a painted-on effect that felt authentic to the exhibition. The result was a dynamic and immersive experience that blended historical accuracy with artistic innovation, enriching the way visitors engaged with the collection.
Highlights – Over 85,000 visitors engaged with the exhibition, experiencing history in motion and proving how digital storytelling can deepen cultural connections.

data.meta_description: Bringing ancient Greek artifacts to life through dynamic experiential storytelling.

data.title: Climate Journey

summary.text: Turning complex carbon data into a dynamic, interactive experience to drive real change.

description.text: Sustainability reporting is no longer a nice-to-have, it’s becoming an expectation from clients, regulators, and stakeholders. Sweep offers businesses unparalleled carbon tracking data, but making this information clear, actionable, and engaging required a fresh approach. We collaborated to transform their reporting into an interactive, visually dynamic experience that drives real impact.

For organisations to truly engage with sustainability data, they need more than static reports. We worked closely with Sweep to craft an intuitive, design-led experience where businesses can explore their carbon footprint as a living, evolving digital landscape - packed with animated insights, clear visual cues, and gamified interactions.

By visualising their sustainability data in their organisation’s own illustrated island, we gave them a sense of ownership. They could see in real time how decisions they made affected their overall carbon footprint, not just in their own organisation, but also in those they choose to work with. Combining clarity with creativity helped Sweep on their mission to position sustainability reporting not only as compliance, but a catalyst for action.
Highlights – A reimagined sustainability report that turns complex data into an interactive journey - giving businesses the tools they need to track, understand, and reduce their carbon impact.

description.text: Phantom is seeking a full-time Designer to join our London team. You will bring raw talent, curiosity, and a strong creative instinct to help us deliver bold, conceptual, and distinctive work for our clients. A true team player, will be generous with ideas and have strong beliefs—held loosely.

As a driving force behind our creative output, you will collaborate within our design team to develop and refine the creative vision of each project, so you must be ready to get stuck in at all levels. Egos are left at the door.
Phantom is a technology focused and creatively driven company, dedicated to elevating brands in the digital realm.
Started by our four co-founders in 2013, we’ve grown into a company 100+ Phantoms strong, with locations spanning across two hemispheres (our other studio in Auckland).

Our partners choose us because of the collaboration, innovation and creativity we all bring to every project. We choose our clients because they’re brands we love to work with, who in turn inspire us to make work we love.

We work on everything from large scale campaigns to creating immersive digital experiences and developing long lasting products. If you’re somebody who enjoys a new challenge each day and is looking to create the best work of your career, Phantom is your place.

You should be comfortable working across various design and illustration aesthetics, with a strong understanding of how static frames translate into animation and broader design projects. While animation skills are a plus, they are not essential.

In short, we are looking for a well-rounded team player to push our design work forward with brilliant creative ideas, exceptional design skills, meticulous attention to detail, and smart strategic thinking.

summary.text: A custom internal Google tool to automate, accelerate, and optimise acquisition marketing workflows.

description.text: Google’s Ads Marketing teams needed a faster, more efficient way to create and track customised marketing journeys. We built Octopus, a powerful internal tool that streamlines the entire process by eliminating inefficiencies and accelerating Google’s ability to test, learn, and optimise campaigns.

Octopus centralised and automated critical marketing data, giving Googlers the ability to build, launch, and refine acquisition journeys in record time. By reducing an 8-week workflow to just 10 minutes, the platform increases speed to market, enabling more frequent campaigns and driving greater revenue impact.

Beyond efficiency, Octopus serves as a unified, secure repository, ensuring seamless compliance with Google’s rigorous data, privacy, and security standards. Every aspect was designed to fit within Google’s unique infrastructure, making complex processes simpler while maintaining full adherence to internal legal and codebase requirements.

Highlights – A game-changing internal tool that radically improved Google’s acquisition process, cutting workflow time from 8 weeks to 10 minutes and driving increased campaign volume, efficiency, and revenue impact.

data.title: Footboo

summary.text: Conjuring up Euros team spirit with an AI-powered football card generator.

description.text: Football fandom is as much about nostalgia as it is about the game itself. For the Euros, we created Footboo, Phantom’s Manifest AI-powered football card generator that let fans see themselves as legends from the 80s, 90s, and 00s. Instantly iconic haircuts, outrageous kits, and a bit of AI magic turned every selfie into a hilariously shareable keepsake.

The best viral experiences are quick, simple, and just unexpected enough to be irresistible. With FootBoo, that meant simply uploading a selfie, picking an era and skin tone, to be delivered a gloriously retro football card in seconds. Whether they ended up with a mullet, a centre parting, or a headband worthy of peak Beckham, every result felt like a nostalgic time capsule of footballing history.

To keep fans coming back, we dropped special edition packs throughout the tournament, celebrating everything from bobbleheads to last-minute equaliser drama. FootBoo took over social feeds, made a full segment on Lorraine, featured on Match of the Day, and even found its way onto BBC Sport.
Highlights – Over four million generations from 800,000 users, with national media coverage and viral traction across football communities, making FootBoo our most successful AI generator yet.

summary.text: Crafting Google Cloud tools that simplify complex regulations and emerging tech for businesses.

description.text: From digital sovereignty regulations to the rise of generative AI, businesses face more complexity than ever. To help them navigate these challenges, we worked with Google Cloud to build two interactive tools, Digital Sovereignty Explorer and Gen AI Navigator, to deliver personalised, easy-to-understand insights.

By answering a short series of questions, businesses receive expert guidance on compliance with digital sovereignty rules in EMEA or explore how to integrate generative AI into their operations. Designed with an intuitive interface, the tools transform technical jargon into accessible, actionable steps.

Built in close collaboration with Google Cloud teams, these tools have become essential resources for businesses navigating regulatory and technological challenges, empowering them to move forward with confidence in an ever-evolving digital landscape.

Highlights – The tools have exceeded expectations in lead generation, engagement, and sentiment, providing businesses with accessible, region-specific guidance while reinforcing Google Cloud’s role as a trusted partner in digital transformation.

description.text:
At Phantom, we are a technology-focused and creatively driven company, dedicated to elevating brands in the digital realm.

Innovation is at the core of what we do, and we embrace AI as a tool to enhance efficiency, insight, and creativity—while ensuring that all creative work remains human-led. 
Our approach to AI is guided by transparency, responsibility, and ethical best practices to maintain the highest standards in everything we deliver.
AI is never a substitute for human creativity but may be used for research, automation, or idea enhancement.
If AI is used in a project, we will disclose its role to our clients. We also internally mark AI assets and include relevant sources as per our internal AI policies
All AI-assisted work is reviewed and approved by our team to maintain originality, accuracy, and compliance with legal and ethical standards.
Our AI practices align with the laws of England and Wales:
UK AI Regulation – We follow the UK’s evolving pro-innovation AI approach, ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability Here

Data Protection & Privacy – We comply with the Data Protection Act 2018 
(UK GDPR) ensuring responsible AI use in relation to personal data. Here
Intellectual Property (IP) & Copyright – AI-generated content follows UK copyright law, and we aim to not infringe third-party rights. Here

primary.label: International Best Practices (For clients outside the UK)

description.text: While our business is governed by English law, we recognise that international clients may operate under different AI regulations, such as:
EU AI Act – We monitor and adapt to ensure compliance for projects involving EU-based businesses. Here
US AI Frameworks – We monitor AI governance developments in the US, including federal and state-specific regulations. Here
Other Regions – We consider international AI policies when working with clients outside the UK.
At Phantom, we recognise that AI models can inherit and amplify biases from the data they are trained on. We take proactive steps to identify, mitigate, and minimise bias in any AI-assisted work:
Human Oversight & Review – All AI-supported content is checked for fairness, accuracy, and inclusivity before being shared or published.

Ethical AI Practices – We carefully select AI tools that prioritise bias reduction and diversity-aware training methodologies and where possible, we fine-tune models to further enhance fairness and inclusivity
Diverse & Representative Inputs – Where applicable, we ensure that AI-driven insights are drawn from varied, high-quality, and representative datasets.
Continuous Learning & Adjustment – AI bias is an evolving challenge, and we remain committed to ongoing evaluation, auditing, and refinement of AI-assisted processes.
We do not use AI to mislead, deceive, or infringe on rights.
AI will only be used in ways that align with our values of originality, integrity, and creativity.
We regularly review AI tools to ensure compliance with ethical and legal standards.
For any questions about our AI use, please contact us at ai@phantom.land

primary.title: Modern Slavery and Human Trafficking Statement

description.text: At Phantom we are committed to preventing modern slavery, human trafficking, forced labour, and exploitation in all aspects of our business and supply chain. We recognise our responsibility to ensure ethical working practices and uphold human rights across our operations.

Phantom Studios Ltd is a digital agency operating in the UK and New Zealand providing services in creative marketing, AI-driven solutions and  technology development. We work with a network of clients, suppliers, and partners globally, and we are committed to maintaining transparency and integrity in all our business relationships.
To mitigate the risk of modern slavery, we have implemented the following measures:
Supplier Code of Conduct – Ensuring all partners adhere to fair labour practices.
Contractual Obligations – Embedding ethical clauses in agreements with vendors, freelancers, and third parties.
Employee Awareness – Providing training on recognising and reporting modern slavery risks.

primary.label: Risk Assessment and Supply Chain Management

description.text: We assess risks associated with our supply chain, particularly when working with third-party vendors, offshore providers, or industries where modern slavery risks are higher. Our due diligence process includes periodic reviews and ethical sourcing commitments.
We are dedicated to continuously reviewing and improving our approach to tackling modern slavery. This includes regular policy updates, supplier audits, and engagement with industry best practices.
If any employee, supplier, or third party suspects an issue related to modern slavery within our business or supply chain, we encourage prompt reporting via privacy@phantom.land.
This statement is made pursuant to the Modern Slavery Act 2015

The process will likely be led by the person you would be reporting into. However, throughout the whole process you can expect to meet anyone from our leadership team, right through to those you’ll be working closely with day to day, sometimes even from different departments. You’ll be able to ask questions along the way and get a good sense of what it's like to be part of the team.
